newsitem.title: BULGARIA: IMF postpones Bulgaria funding by one month.
newsitem.headline: IMF postpones Bulgaria funding by one month.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) postponed a second $115 million tranche of funding until Bulgaria completes reform pledges and its stabilisation measures show results, the finance minister said on Saturday.

"We have agreed on an IMF mission visit by the end of October, which will conclude the programme review and set the parameters for next year," Dimitar Kostov told reporters on arrival from the annual IMF/World Bank meeting in Washington.
The IMF postponed the loan until the government fulfilled its pledges to close 64 loss-making state enterprises and speed up privatisation.
"The fund approved of Bulgaria's latest stabilisation measures, but it is necessary to see how will they work and what will be their long-term effect," said Kostov.

Two weeks ago Bulgaria's central bank placed nine banks under special supervision and hiked interest rates to an all-time high of 300 percent in a bid to stabilise the crumbling financial system and the national currency.
"It is important to know on what assumptions to draft the budget frame for 1997 and sustain a long-term stability," said Kostov, speaking after discussions with IMF senior management on Friday.
"Our priority is to curb inflation which was spurred by the banking crisis," he added.
Pegging the lev or introducing a fixed rate in the current unstable situation would not produce positive results and was not on the agenda, said Kostov.
Other reform pledges included selling off up to 20 state enterprises by year-end. Along with the IMF tranche, Bulgaria also hoped to win funding from the World Bank in November, he said.
"It is important to receive the tranche by year-end as the next big foreign debt payment is in January," said Kostov.
If Bulgaria completes reform pledges, the IMF may disburse in November the second and third tranche, together worth around $200 million, said an IMF official.
Under a reform package sealed with the IMF in July, Bulgaria stands to receive $580 million over 20 months if it meets reform targets.
